title: ITR-U updated return: how to fix a missed or wrong return years later
seoTitle: ITR-U Updated Return: Open Years, Extra Tax, How to File
h1: ITR-U updated return: how to fix a missed or wrong return years later
metaDescription: ITR-U updated return explained: which years are open in October 2026, the 25–70% extra tax, how to file on the portal, and what to do if you're owed a refund.
excerpt: Missed income or a whole return? Which years ITR-U still covers, what the extra charge costs, how to file it, and why it can't get you a refund.
targetAudience: Indian taxpayers who missed income or a return in an earlier year
sourceVideoTitle: ❌ Don't file Updated Return (ITR-U) | How to file updated return | How to file ITR 2026
author: Muthu

faq.question: Who can file an updated return?
faq.answer: Anyone who wants to report more income or correct a return for an open year, whether or not they filed a return for that year. It's not allowed if it would lower your tax, increase a refund or loss, if you've already filed an updated return for that year, or if a search or survey has started.

faq.question: How many years back can I file ITR-U?
faq.answer: Up to 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year. As of October 2026 that covers FY 2021-22 to FY 2024-25. FY 2021-22 closes on 31 March 2027.

faq.question: How much extra tax do I pay with ITR-U?
faq.answer: 25% of the tax plus interest if you file within 12 months of the end of the assessment year, 50% within 24 months, 60% within 36 months and 70% within 48 months. After a reassessment notice, another 10% is added.

faq.question: Can I claim a refund through ITR-U?
faq.answer: No. An updated return can't create or increase a refund. If you're owed money for a year you didn't file, apply for condonation of delay through the e-filing portal instead.

faq.question: Can I file ITR-U for FY 2025-26?
faq.answer: You don't need to yet. A belated or revised return for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) can be filed until 31 December 2026, and it costs a late fee and interest rather than the extra ITR-U charge.
